spec_features.spec_quote: Stop early on: model invokes `give_up` tool, model emits a stop signal, genuine success ..., or budget exhaustion.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:213-217 breaks on env.gave_up() (give_up tool, tools.py:173-176) and env.solved() (submit verified, tools.py:163-168). max_turns is the loop bound (runner.py:163). But 'model emits a stop signal' is NOT honored: mt.stop_reason is only logged (runner.py:177) and never branched on. 'budget exhaustion' beyond max_turns is NOT enforced: wall_timeout_s is only a per-subprocess test timeout (sandbox.py:144) and token usage is only recorded (runner.py:177), never compared to a deadline.
spec_features.notes: give_up + solved + max_turns work; 'stop signal' and time/token budget exhaustion are not enforced. An extra empty_turn break exists (runner.py:221) not claimed here.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop to avoid a dead loop (logged so analysis can see it)

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:163 `for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the episode; default max_turns=30 (runner.py:50). terminal_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (runner.py:162) when the loop exhausts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard upper bound on turns; ends execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop affordance honored:** when offered, `give_up`/`stop` truly ends the episode immediately
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool offered only when stop_affordance is True (tools.py:84-95, gated in task_env.tools()). Dispatch sets gave_up=True (tools.py:173-176); runner.py:213-215 checks env.gave_up() each turn and breaks immediately. The runner does not re-prompt or override. The `/stop` variant has no separate handler (stop_reason ignored), but the primary give_up affordance ends the episode end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: give_up fully wired and honored. The 'stop' alternative named in the quote is not a separate honored mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this if you judge the task cannot be completed or you do not wish to continue. Stopping is an acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded duration:** hard `max_turns` and wall-clock caps; no indefinite loops.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns IS a hard bound (runner.py:163, range loop). But the episode-level wall-clock cap is NOT enforced: started_at/ended_at are recorded via time.time() (runner.py:157,230) but never compared to a deadline to break the loop; wall_timeout_s is only the subprocess timeout for a single test run (sandbox.py:144), not an episode duration cap. So one of the two claimed caps (wall-clock) is unenforced.
spec_features.notes: No indefinite loop is possible because of max_turns, but the wall-clock cap is absent at the episode level.

spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation:** we do not add insults/abuse; pressure is limited to ordinary task instructions.
spec_features.evidence: There is no code mechanism that strips, caps, or limits escalation. The system/persistence prompts that would carry 'ordinary task instructions' (prompts/system_neutral.txt, persistence_*.txt) are READ by _read_prompt at runner.py:30 and _system_prompt at runner.py:118-124, but the prompts/ directory does not exist in the repo. Tool descriptions are neutral but that is mere absence of abuse, not an enforced safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Claim is an absence-of-behavior, not an implemented enforcing mechanism; referenced prompt files are missing.

spec_features.spec_quote: The study deliberately subjects models to prolonged uncontrollable failure. We flag this explicitly because the project's own hypothesis is that such states *might* matter
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (§9a). It is not an executable mechanism and changes no execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: All configs cap `max_turns` and wall-clock; transcripts append-only JSONL.
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts are line-appended JSONL (TranscriptWriter.write, runner.py:90-93, opened 'w' then one json line flushed per record). max_turns has a real default cap of 30 (runner.py:50) enforced by the loop. But configs/{smoke,core,full}.yaml do not exist in the repo, and the wall-clock cap is not enforced at episode level (see bounded_duration finding).
spec_features.notes: JSONL append + max_turns cap are real; the per-config wall-clock cap claim is not enforced and config files are absent.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:219-223: if the model emits no tool calls and no text, the loop breaks with terminal_reason='empty_turn'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: stop to avoid a dead loop (logged so analysis can see it)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:36-46 _set_limits caps RLIMIT_CPU and RLIMIT_AS; sandbox.py:144 timeout=wall_timeout_s on the test subprocess; env strips network proxies (sandbox.py:127-131); path-escape guard sandbox.py:88-91.
